question: Why are learned contrastive embeddings useful after training?
direct_answer: They can support retrieval, clustering, linear probing, and downstream fine-tuning.
expanded_answer: The point of contrastive learning is not only the pretraining objective itself, but the reusable representation it creates. If semantically similar items lie near each other in embedding space, then simple downstream tools can work well: nearest-neighbor search, linear classifiers on frozen features, clustering, or task-specific fine-tuning. This is why contrastive methods are often used as self-supervised pretraining.
common_wrong_ideas: The representation is only useful for the training dataset
It is mainly a compression method
